articles.body: Hapag-Lloyd further raises its earnings outlook for the current financial year in International Shipping News 11/11/2026 Supported by continued robust spot freight rates, business performance in the fourth quarter is developing better than previously expected. The Executive Board of Hapag-Lloyd AG therefore decided today to raise its earnings outlook for the 2026 financial year once again. Group EBITDA is now expected to be in the range of USD 4.6 to 5.0 billion (previously: USD 3.9 to 4.4 billion) and Group EBIT in the range of USD 2.0 to 2.4 billion (previously: USD 1.25 to 1.75 billion). In Euro, this corresponds to an expected Group EBITDA of EUR 4.0 to 4.4 billion (previously: EUR 3.4 to 3.8 billion) and Group EBIT of EUR 1.7 to 2.1 billion (previously: EUR 1.1 to 1.5 billion). Against the backdrop of volatile freight rates and persistent geopolitical challenges, the forecast is subject to a considerable degree of uncertainty. The Quarterly Financial Report for the first nine months of 2026 will be published as scheduled on 12 November 2026. Source: Hapag-Lloyd 2026-11-11 hellenicshippingnews... tweet Share

articles.title: French-speaking countries strengthen readiness for upcoming IMO audit cycle
articles.summary: Maritime administrations from 13 French-speaking countries are enhancing their preparedness for the next audit cycle under the IMO Member State Audit Scheme (IMSAS). A regional workshop in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire (9-13 November), led by IMO in cooperation with the General Directorate of Maritime Affairs of Côte...
articles.body: French-speaking countries strengthen readiness for upcoming IMO audit cycle in International Shipping News 11/11/2026 Maritime administrations from 13 French-speaking countries are enhancing their preparedness for the next audit cycle under the IMO Member State Audit Scheme (IMSAS). A regional workshop in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire (9-13 November), led by IMO in cooperation with the General Directorate of Maritime Affairs of Côte d’Ivoire, brings together maritime administrations and Single Points of Contact (SPCs) – the designated official or unit appointed by a Member State to act as the primary liaison between the country and the IMO audit team – from 13 French-speaking Member States. Preparing for the second audit cycle Ahead of the commencement of the second audit cycle in July 2027, the workshop is based on the revised Framework and Procedures for IMSAS (resolution A.1211(34)). Participants are examining key changes to the audit process, including the introduction of the IMO Continuous Monitoring Mechanism (ICMM) and a risk-based approach to audit prioritization. The training also focuses on the practical and administrative arrangements required for effective audit preparation and implementation. Topics include the Audit Standard (III Code), the Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC), the State Audit Questionnaire (SAQ), the Verification Index, and gap analysis using the Non-exhaustive List of Obligations (resolution A.1208(34)). By strengthening national capacities and promoting continuous improvement, the workshop supports sustained compliance with applicable IMO instruments and enhances Member States’ ability to meet their international obligations. Organized under IMO’s Integrated Technical Cooperation Programme (ITCP), the activity forms part of the thematic programme on improving compliance with international maritime standards through IMSAS. The workshop reflects IMO’s commitment to gender inclusion, with women accounting for 31% of participants. Source: IMO 2026-11-11 hellenicshippingnews... tweet Share

articles.body: Rough weather disrupts bunkering in Gibraltar Strait and wider region in Port News 11/11/2026 Rough weather has delayed bunkering in the Gibraltar Strait and suspended it in Huelva and at Las Palmas’ outer anchorage. Storm Charles has brought strong winds, heavy rain and rough seas to southern and western Spain, the Gibraltar Strait and the Canary Islands this week. In Gibraltar and Algeciras, rough westerly winds of around 25 knots are forecast in the port throughout the day and tomorrow. This has prompted Gibraltar Port Authority to issue a severe weather warning. Gibraltar’s vessel traffic service will suspend inbound traffic because of the weather warning, port agent MH Bland said. Bunker operations outside port limits can continue for now, it added. Eight vessels are waiting for bunkers in Gibraltar, according to MH Bland. Suppliers are running anywhere between 4-14 hours late on deliveries as of now. The delays could increase due to the suspension. In neighbouring Algeciras, inbound movements at the inner anchorage have been suspended due to rough winds, MH Bland said. The bunker-focused outer Delta anchorage is open. Some suppliers could face delays of about a day, the port agent said. Bunker operations have been suspended at Las Palmas’ outer anchorage, where winds are blowing at around 25 knots and waves are reaching 1.5 metres, MH Bland said. Deliveries are still possible at berth and at the inner anchorage, but with some delays. Bunker operations are also expected to be suspended in Tenerife for at least two days. In Huelva, rough weather has suspended bunker operations since Monday. Only one bunker barge serves the port, so delays could follow as deliveries are rescheduled. articles.body: Saudi Arabia opens anti-dumping probe into steel imports from China, Turkiye in Commodity News 11/11/2026 Saudi Arabia’s General Authority for Foreign Trade has announced the initiation of an anti-dumping investigation into the Kingdom’s imports of “hot-rolled iron or steel structural sections, angles, and shapes (light and medium categories)” originating in or exported from China and Turkiye. The decision to launch the investigation was made in accordance with the Trade Remedies Law in International Trade, issued on Nov. 23, 2022, the Saudi Press Agency reported. Article 4, Paragraph 1 of the law stipulates that the authority is responsible for trade remedy functions, including conducting investigations and reviews, and imposing measures, in compliance with the Kingdom’s international commitments, specifically the Anti-Dumping Agreement, the Agreement on Subsidies and Countervailing Measures, and the Agreement on Safeguards. The law aims to protect domestic industries from injury caused by dumped or subsidized imports, safeguard against increases in imports, and defend the Kingdom’s exports that may be subject to trade remedy measures by other nations. For further details about the investigation, GAFT said interested parties can visit its official website at https://gaft.gov.sa, specifically the “Announcements and Circulars for Trade Remedy Investigations” or “Details of Ongoing Investigations and Reviews” sections. articles.summary: The average rate on a 30-year fixed US mortgage fell 9 basis points to 7.21% in the week ending November 6, marking a fourth consecutive weekly decline and providing some relief to the struggling housing market. Borrowing costs have dropped nearly 30 basis points from an almost two-year high of 7.5% reached early...
articles.body: US 30-Year Mortgage Rates Fall for 4th Week in World Economy News 11/11/2026 The average rate on a 30-year fixed US mortgage fell 9 basis points to 7.21% in the week ending November 6, marking a fourth consecutive weekly decline and providing some relief to the struggling housing market. Borrowing costs have dropped nearly 30 basis points from an almost two-year high of 7.5% reached early last month, although rates remain elevated enough to deter many prospective buyers. Lower financing costs helped drive a 7.5% increase in mortgage applications for home purchases, the largest weekly gain since mid-April and only the second rise since late August. Applications for refinancing also increased 4.5%, extending their advance to a third consecutive week, although the index remains near its lowest level since January 2025. Despite these improvements, a sustained decline in borrowing costs may be necessary to encourage stronger housing activity. Contract signings for previously owned homes fell to a record low in September following a sharp rise in mortgage rates. Source: Trading Economics 2026-11-11 hellenicshippingnews... tweet Share

articles.title: RCL to deploy two new 7,000-TEU vessels on Asia-India service
articles.summary: Regional Container Lines (RCL) is preparing to introduce two new 7,000-TEU container vessels into its regional shipping network, with both ships scheduled for delivery in January 2027. The Thai container shipping company held naming ceremonies for KITIYA BHUM and LAKANA BHUM on 10 November in Shanghai, China, as part...
articles.body: Regional Container Lines (RCL) is preparing to introduce two new 7,000-TEU container vessels into its regional shipping network, with both ships scheduled for delivery in January 2027. The Thai container shipping company held naming ceremonies for KITIYA BHUM and LAKANA BHUM on 10 November in Shanghai, China, as part of its ongoing fleet renewal and expansion programme. The vessels are planned for deployment on RCL’s Korea Straits-India Service 2 (RKI2), which connects ports in South Korea, China, Malaysia, India and Pakistan, supporting container trade between Northeast Asia and the Indian Subcontinent. New vessels equipped with efficiency and emissions technologies According to RCL, both vessels have been built by Shanghai Waigaoqiao Shipbuilding (SWS), with naming ceremonies held at HantongWING Shipyard and Rongsheng Shipyard, respectively. Each vessel has a nominal capacity of 7,000 TEU and incorporates several technologies intended to improve operational efficiency and environmental performance. These include energy-saving devices (ESD), exhaust gas cleaning systems (EGCS), selective catalytic reduction (SCR) technology and alternative maritime power (AMP) capabilities, allowing the ships to connect to shore-based electricity where suitable infrastructure is available. The equipment is designed to improve energy efficiency and support compliance with applicable emissions requirements. Fleet expansion supports regional network development The planned introduction of KITIYA BHUM and LAKANA BHUM forms part of RCL’s broader fleet rejuvenation strategy, which focuses on replacing and expanding tonnage while improving operational capabilities across its shipping network. Their deployment on the RKI2 service will add modern vessel capacity to a trade corridor linking Northeast Asian manufacturing centres with markets across South and Southeast Asia. RCL said it would continue investing in fleet renewal and operational efficiency as it develops its regional container shipping services.

articles.title: Georgia emerges as a centre of excellence for automotive manufacturing and logistics
articles.summary: Georgia Ports Authority hosted its annual State of the Port of Brunswick, where CEO Griff Lynch and President Kevin Price reviewed market conditions and future plans. They pointed to the state’s success in attracting global automakers and building supply chains around them, following Audi’s recent announcement of a...
articles.body: Georgia Ports Authority hosted its annual State of the Port of Brunswick, where CEO Griff Lynch and President Kevin Price reviewed market conditions and future plans. They pointed to the state’s success in attracting global automakers and building supply chains around them, following Audi’s recent announcement of a factory in Georgia. Hyundai Motor Group’s Metaplant at Ellabell, 30 miles west of the Port of Savannah, occupies a 3,000-acre site and will create 8,500 jobs by 2031, with 22 suppliers already located nearby. Kia has run its flagship US plant at West Point on 2,200 acres since 2009. Rivian has broken ground on a USD 5 billion plant at Stanton Springs North, expected to create 7,500 long-term jobs by 2030, and has set up its East Coast headquarters in Atlanta. Audi plans to invest US$ 4 billion in its first US plant, near Macon, one of the brand’s largest production footprints globally, with about 4,500 jobs. Construction is due to start in 2027 and production in the early 2030s. BMW, Mercedes-Benz and Volvo, among others, use the Port of Brunswick for finished vehicle shipments and processing. The ports’ appeal to manufacturers and logistics providers rests on the combination of seaport access, dedicated rail, direct interstate links and proximity to Southeastern markets. Brunswick provides vehicle imports and exports, finished vehicle distribution, parts warehousing, manufacturing and vehicle processing. Savannah is a major gateway for containerised auto parts, with 40 vessel calls a week, 15,000 daily truck gate transactions and 42 double-stack trains a week from its on-dock Mason Mega Rail facility to inland markets via Norfolk Southern and CSX. Atlanta adds a major consumer market and distribution hub. Price also noted strong growth in heavy machinery such as construction and farm equipment. Lynch said Georgia Ports are creating opportunities for businesses to grow, strengthening supply chain competitiveness at state, regional, national and global levels and generating jobs. Chairman Alec Poitevint noted that Georgia has been named best state to do business for 13 consecutive years and that GPA is investing US$ 5 billion in infrastructure over the next ten years to meet future demand. Lynch and Price thanked GPA employees, the board, the ILA, customers and the local community.

articles.title: Maersk hit by fresh cyber breach
articles.summary: Danish shipping giant AP Moller-Maersk has confirmed another cybersecurity breach after hackers gained access to an older IT system and extracted data, nearly a decade after the devastating NotPetya attack that cost the company up to $300m. The Copenhagen-headquartered group said on Wednesday that the incident...
articles.body: Containers Europe Maersk hit by fresh cyber breach Adis Ajdin November 12, 2026 0 91 1 minute read Cydome Cydome Danish shipping giant AP Moller-Maersk has confirmed another cybersecurity breach after hackers gained access to an older IT system and extracted data, nearly a decade after the devastating NotPetya attack that cost the company up to $300m. The Copenhagen-headquartered group said on Wednesday that the incident involved a local legacy system inherited through a previous acquisition. Maersk’s cybersecurity team launched an investigation after discovering the intrusion and has taken steps to secure the affected system.”Our findings so far strongly suggest no sensitive data has been disclosed,” the company said. The carrier said the breach appeared to be confined to the legacy system, with no indication that other Maersk systems or those belonging to customers and partners connected through APIs and electronic data interchange (EDI) had been compromised. The company added that it does not expect disruption to customer operations, with its digital booking and shipment management platforms continuing to operate normally. Maersk has not identified the acquired business involved, disclosed what data was extracted or named those responsible for the intrusion. The announcement follows separate claims by a hacker group calling itself WhiteArmor that it had obtained around 100 GB of logistics data from a platform associated with LF Logistics, the Hong Kong-based logistics business Maersk acquired for $3.6bn in 2022. The group has reportedly demanded $5m in bitcoin. The claims remain unverified, and Maersk has not confirmed any connection between the alleged theft and the incident it is investigating. The latest breach brings back memories of June 2017, when the NotPetya malware attack crippled Maersk’s IT infrastructure and disrupted container shipping and terminal operations worldwide. The Danish group subsequently put the financial damage at between $250m and $300m, making it one of the costliest cyber incidents in shipping history. The New York-listed owner disclosed the agreement with an unnamed Asian leasing company in its third-quarter update. The deal covers the 2018-built, 173,400 cu m Flex Enterprise , which will be sold to the lessor and chartered back on a bareboat basis for approximately six years. The financing carries an age-adjusted repayment profile of around 21 years and includes an option for Flex to repurchase the vessel at a fixed price after roughly six years. Flex said it intends to use the proceeds to repay the outstanding balance on its existing $150m Flex Enterprise financing facility, which matures in June 2029. Once the existing debt has been cleared, the company expects the refinancing to release approximately $34m in net cash. The transaction is due to close before the end of 2026. The latest deal comes after Flex renegotiated the terms of an existing $330m sale-and-leaseback covering Flex Artemis and Flex Amber in October. Flex operates 13 LNG carriers and has steadily been reshaping its debt through bank loans and leasing arrangements. Last year, the company completed similar transactions involving Flex Resolute, Flex Courageous and Flex Constellation. articles.body: Americas Middle East Operations Regulatory Tankers Canada puts Iranian tanker giant back under sanctions Adis Ajdin November 12, 2026 0 36 1 minute read Canada has reinstated sanctions against the National Iranian Tanker Company (NITC), reversing relief granted a decade ago under the international nuclear agreement with Tehran. The move forms part of a package targeting 11 Iranian entities, including National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC), oil trading group Naftiran Intertrade and several major financial institutions. The measures were announced by Canadian foreign minister Anita Anand during a G7 foreign ministers’ meeting in Paris. The restrictions prohibit specified dealings involving the property of sanctioned entities and related financial services by people and businesses in Canada, as well as Canadians operating abroad. The decision puts NITC back under Canadian restrictions for the first time since February 2016, when Ottawa removed the company and several other Iranian organisations from its sanctions list following implementation of the nuclear agreement. NITC is one of the world’s major crude tanker operators and a central player in Iran’s seaborne oil exports. The company already faces extensive US restrictions, with tankers associated with its operations repeatedly targeted under measures aimed at limiting Iran’s oil revenues. Canada said the latest action follows renewed concerns over Iran’s nuclear programme and cooperation with international inspectors. The decision comes after United Nations nuclear-related sanctions were reinstated in September 2025. The government said the renewed listings are intended to further restrict Iranian access to financial resources and sensitive technologies. REUTERS/Amr Alfiky/File Photo International Maritime Organization (IMO) Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez has called on governments to step up enforcement of international maritime regulations in the Strait of Hormuz, warning that unsafe shipping practices are adding to the risks facing seafarers amid the ongoing conflict. In a statement issued Wednesday, Dominguez raised concerns about vessels transiting the strategic waterway without complying with basic international safety requirements, including provisions of the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS). The warning comes as commercial shipping continues to face attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz, where the IMO has now verified more than 130 incidents involving merchant vessels since the conflict began on February 28. At least 25 seafarers have been killed, while others remain missing or have been injured. “IMO’s technical and operational regulations are there to protect seafarers, ships and the marine environment. They must be respected and enforced effectively,” Dominguez said. The IMO chief specifically cited reports of substandard vessels, ships concealing their IMO identification numbers, vessels operating under fraudulent registrations or false flags, and other unsafe practices. The concerns add another dimension to the shipping crisis in the Persian Gulf, where vessels already face significant security risks from ongoing hostilities. Dominguez’s comments highlight the need for governments to enforce existing maritime regulations even as the conflict complicates commercial navigation. He called on flag states, port states and coastal states to take action against violations within their respective jurisdictions and in accordance with international law. “I strongly urge shipowners and operators to refrain from commercial activities in the Strait that expose seafarers to unacceptable risks,” Dominguez said. The latest appeal follows last week’s meeting of the IMO Council in London, where member states called for stronger protections for seafarers and reiterated that vital shipping lanes must remain open, safe and secure. During the November 2–6 meeting, the Council condemned attacks on merchant shipping and called on governments to refrain from unlawful measures that endanger seafarers and international navigation. According to the IMO’s latest incident records, 133 incidents had been confirmed as of November 10, with 25 seafarer fatalities. Dominguez also renewed his call for a political solution to the crisis, urging governments to restore a safe, internationally recognized framework for navigation through the Strait of Hormuz that preserves established rights and freedoms of navigation. He warned that the conflict’s consequences extend well beyond the maritime industry, contributing to higher living costs for millions of people worldwide. “It is imperative for Governments to tackle the root causes of this conflict,” he said. Join the leading maritime news network Photo courtesy Panama Canal Authority The Panama Canal is increasing its daily transit capacity to 34 vessels and restoring the maximum allowable draft at its Neopanamax locks to 50 feet, easing restrictions as improved water conditions provide some relief from concerns over another prolonged El Niño. The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) announced the changes in a November 9 advisory to shipping, citing improving lake levels, favorable hydrological forecasts and the effectiveness of water-saving measures implemented at the locks. The adjustment adds one daily booking slot for Super vessels at the Panamax locks, increasing availability in that category from 18 to 19. Total daily reservation capacity rises from 33 to 34 slots, including 24 at the Panamax locks and 10 at the larger Neopanamax locks. The ACP also raised the maximum authorized draft for Neopanamax vessels to 15.24 meters (50 feet), effective immediately and until further notice. The increase follows an October adjustment that raised the allowable draft to 49 feet. The latest changes mark another shift in the canal’s operating outlook after months of concern over deteriorating water conditions and the potential for a prolonged El Niño event. As gCaptain reported in September, canal officials had postponed a planned reduction in the Neopanamax draft limit to 47.5 feet after reassessing Gatun Lake levels and rainfall projections. At the time, the canal was maintaining a 48-foot draft limit while warning that below-normal precipitation could persist for months. The concerns followed the historic 2023–2024 drought , which forced the canal to sharply restrict vessel transits and drafts, disrupting global shipping schedules and sending some cargoes on longer routes. At the worst point of that drought, daily transit capacity fell to just 22 vessels. The waterway has faced additional pressure this year as disruptions in the Middle East have redirected shipping traffic toward Panama, increasing competition for available transit reservations, particularly among energy carriers. The additional Panamax booking slot will be introduced in stages. For transit dates November 12–17, it will be available through the canal’s auction system. For November 18–23, it will be offered through the Special Competition booking period. Beginning with November 24 transit dates, the slot will become available through the regular Second Competition Period. Despite the improved outlook, the ACP continues to emphasize the importance of advance reservations. Its Transit Reservation System remains the only way to guarantee a transit date, and vessels arriving without bookings could face substantial delays. The authority said it will continue monitoring rainfall, watershed conditions and lake levels, with further operational adjustments possible as conditions change. The latest increase offers shipping companies greater flexibility heading into the final weeks of 2026, although the canal’s ability to sustain the higher capacity will continue to depend on freshwater availability. Join the leading maritime news network Illustration courtesy Ocean Infinity The UK is moving ahead with a £90 million investment in autonomous underwater systems, advanced sensors and artificial intelligence to strengthen the Royal Navy’s ability to track Russian submarines and protect critical infrastructure in the North Atlantic. The initiative, known as Atlantic Net, is the first operational phase of the Royal Navy’s broader Atlantic Bastion programme, which aims to combine crewed warships and submarines with autonomous systems to improve underwater surveillance and counter potential threats to subsea communications cables, energy networks and shipping routes. The UK Ministry of Defence announced the investment Tuesday during the International Sea Power Conference in Oslo, Norway, alongside a framework agreement with UK-based marine robotics company Ocean Infinity Solutions. GOV.UK Under the arrangement, Ocean Infinity will serve as the Royal Navy’s commercial mission partner, helping develop and operate a network of autonomous and remotely operated systems capable of maintaining persistent surveillance across the North Atlantic. The system will combine underwater sensors, uncrewed platforms, communications technology and AI-powered data analysis to detect and track potentially hostile submarine activity. The information will provide Royal Navy warships and Astute-class attack submarines with earlier warnings and a clearer picture of threats beneath the surface. The programme is expected to become operational in 2027, according to UK Defence Minister Luke Pollard, who outlined the plans in a speech in Oslo. “The threats beneath the North Atlantic are changing, and we are changing with them,” Pollard said. “This investment gives the Royal Navy new technology to find threats earlier and protect our critical infrastructure, while also backing British business.” The investment comes amid growing concern among European governments and NATO allies over the vulnerability of underwater infrastructure, particularly communications cables and energy connections that are essential to both civilian economies and military operations. Atlantic Bastion is intended to expand the Navy’s ability to monitor these networks while strengthening anti-submarine warfare capabilities and supporting the protection of Britain’s nuclear deterrent. For Ocean Infinity, the agreement marks a significant expansion of its role in defense and maritime security. The company, which has developed autonomous and remotely operated marine systems for commercial operations, said Atlantic Net represents a shift toward sustained underwater surveillance using a combination of uncrewed, autonomous and smaller-crewed platforms. “The Royal Navy has been exploring how to move beyond traditional, heavily crewed fleets towards a broader mix of robotic and lean-crewed platforms,” said Joe Robinson, President of Solutions at Ocean Infinity. “Atlantic Net is that idea coming to life.” Ocean Infinity said its role will include integrating maritime platforms, underwater sensors, communications, remote operations and data services into a coordinated surveillance capability directed by the Royal Navy. Ocean Infinity The £90 million framework is also expected to support nearly 200 skilled jobs within Ocean Infinity and its immediate supply chain, according to the Ministry of Defence. The programme will operate alongside NATO and Joint Expeditionary Force allies, with the goal of expanding the scale and persistence of underwater surveillance across the North Atlantic. The announcement also forms part of a broader British push toward a hybrid naval fleet that uses autonomous technology to supplement traditional warships and submarines, allowing the Royal Navy to monitor larger areas without relying entirely on crewed vessels. articles.title: Eimskip posts 43.6% EBITDA growth in third quarter
articles.summary: Icelandic shipping and logistics company Eimskip reported a 43.6% year-on-year increase in EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026, supported by higher cargo volumes, stronger freight rates and operational efficiency measures, despite a sharp rise in fuel costs. The company’s quarterly revenue increased by 19.4%...
articles.body: Icelandic shipping and logistics company Eimskip reported a 43.6% year-on-year increase in EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026, supported by higher cargo volumes, stronger freight rates and operational efficiency measures, despite a sharp rise in fuel costs. The company’s quarterly revenue increased by 19.4% compared with the same period in 2025, while EBITDA rose by EUR 8.9 million. Eimskip attributed the improvement to stronger underlying operations and restructuring initiatives introduced during the second half of last year. The year-on-year EBITDA comparison was also influenced by a EUR 2.9 million loss associated with the sale of the vessel Lagarfoss in the third quarter of 2025. Liner volumes rise as network adjustments support operations Eimskip’s liner segment recorded a 13.8% increase in revenue, while transported volumes grew by 6.8%, supported by stronger exports of seafood and farmed fish from Iceland and the Faroe Islands. The company introduced a new connection between Tórshavn in the Faroe Islands and Rotterdam in August, including a call at Ålesund, Norway. The service was established to accommodate increasing farmed salmon production and demand for improved connections to European markets. Alongside the new route, Eimskip adjusted its Norwegian sailing schedule and reduced the number of vessels deployed on that service by one. Despite the improvement in liner operations, profitability remained limited, with the segment generating EBIT of approximately EUR 500,000 during the quarter. “Despite this improvement, profitability remains unsatisfactory,” said Vilhelm Már Thorsteinsson, CEO of Eimskip. Forwarding and logistics contribute to revenue growth Eimskip’s forwarding business recorded a 30% increase in revenue, driven by an 11.2% rise in transported volumes and higher international freight rates. Growth was particularly strong on routes connected to Asia. Revenue from logistics and agency services increased by 14.4%, primarily reflecting greater trucking activity in Iceland, increased warehousing operations and improved port-related results. The company’s new chilled and frozen storage facility in Denmark also contributed to the segment’s performance. Meanwhile, operating expenses increased by 16.7% year-on-year, reflecting higher activity levels, increased third-party transportation costs and rising oil prices. Vessel bunker expenses climbed by EUR 6.1 million, representing a 56% increase compared with the previous year. Eimskip noted that the increase remained below the 78% rise in market fuel prices, mainly due to the timing of bunker purchases. Efficiency measures deliver further savings Operational improvement initiatives introduced in the second half of 2025 generated EUR 3.3 million in benefits during the third quarter, including a positive EBITDA contribution of EUR 2.9 million. For the first nine months of 2026, these initiatives delivered EUR 9.4 million in benefits, including an EBITDA improvement of approximately EUR 8 million. The measures included the discontinuation of dedicated coastal sailings, reductions in vessel deployment and adjustments to the company’s wider operating structure. Eimskip also reported that results from associated companies increased to EUR 7.3 million, compared with EUR 3.5 million a year earlier, primarily reflecting a vessel sale by Elbfeeder in July. Looking ahead, the company expects a more balanced development in working capital during the fourth quarter, following increased requirements associated with higher activity levels in Q3. Eimskip said its priorities remain operational efficiency, cost control and maintaining reliable shipping and logistics services amid continued uncertainty in global markets.

articles.body: CMA CGM has announced new Peak Season Surcharges (PSS) for container shipments from Asia to the Mediterranean, North Africa and Mauritius, with implementation dates scheduled for mid-to-late November 2026. The French shipping company will introduce charges of up to US$1,600 per 40-foot container on Asia–Mediterranean routes. Separate surcharges will apply to shipments from China and other Asian markets to Port Louis, Mauritius. Both measures will remain in effect until further notice. Asia–Mediterranean surcharge takes effect on 25 November From 25 November 2026, CMA CGM will apply a PSS of US$800 per 20-foot container and US$1,600 per 40-foot container on shipments from all major Asian ports to base ports in the Mediterranean and North Africa. The new charges will cover dry containers, refrigerated cargo, out-of-gauge (OOG) shipments and paying empty containers. The implementation date is based on the cargo loading date, with the surcharge remaining in place until further notice. The announcement follows CMA CGM’s earlier adjustments to Asia–Mediterranean freight rates and surcharges for November. The latest measure introduces a separate peak season charge for cargo moving on these routes. Mauritius shipments face revised peak season charges CMA CGM has also announced revised PSS levels for container shipments from the Far East to Port Louis, Mauritius, effective 15 November 2026. Cargo originating in China and its Special Administrative Regions will be subject to a surcharge of US$800 per TEU. Shipments from Northeast Asia and Southeast Asia will face a lower surcharge of US$500 per TEU. Both charges apply to all cargo types and will remain effective until further notice. The revised Mauritius charges follow previous surcharge announcements covering Asia–Africa services . CMA CGM noted that the new surcharges are separate from basic ocean freight rates. Bunker-related charges, terminal handling charges, safety and security fees and other applicable costs may also be added. For shipments originating in China, the carrier said the surcharges will be subject to the relevant filing requirements with the Shanghai Shipping Exchange or may be incorporated into the ocean freight rate. The Mediterranean and North Africa surcharge will also be implemented in accordance with applicable local filing and regulatory requirements. The announcements provide revised pricing conditions for cargo moving from major Asian export markets to Mediterranean and Indian Ocean destinations during the final weeks of 2026.

articles.body: Yang Ming Marine Transport Corporation reported an after-tax net profit of NT$18.57 billion (US$584.75 million) for the third quarter of 2026, supported by stronger cargo demand, higher freight rates and continued capacity constraints across major shipping routes. The Taiwanese container shipping company generated consolidated quarterly revenue of NT$64.15 billion (US$2.02 billion), while earnings per share reached NT$5.32, according to financial results approved by its board on 10 November. For the first nine months of 2026, Yang Ming recorded consolidated revenue of NT$148.73 billion (US$4.68 billion), representing an 18% increase compared with the corresponding period of 2025. After-tax net profit reached NT$25.74 billion (US$810.56 million), with cumulative earnings per share of NT$7.37. Stronger demand and capacity constraints support earnings Yang Ming attributed its financial performance to improving demand across long-haul container shipping trades since the second quarter, with cargo volumes maintaining momentum throughout the traditional third-quarter peak season. Port congestion and the continued diversion of vessels around the Cape of Good Hope further restricted effective shipping capacity, contributing to higher average freight rates. The combination of stronger cargo volumes and improved freight rates supported the carrier’s revenue growth during the first nine months of the year. Fleet expansion expected to outpace demand in 2027 Looking ahead, Yang Ming cited projections from maritime consultancy Drewry indicating that global container shipping capacity will increase by 5% in 2026, compared with demand growth of 3.1%. For 2027, fleet capacity is projected to expand by 8.8%, while demand is expected to grow by 6.2%, suggesting that supply growth will continue to exceed cargo demand. The carrier expects relatively stable demand during the fourth quarter of 2026, with an earlier Lunar New Year potentially encouraging a pre-holiday increase in shipments. However, port congestion could create additional supply chain bottlenecks. Yang Ming identified geopolitical developments, US-China trade policies, port labour negotiations, terminal efficiency and bunker fuel price volatility as key factors influencing the container shipping market. The company also expects environmental regulations, including measures introduced by the European Union and the United Kingdom, to encourage slower vessel operating speeds and the gradual retirement of older ships, potentially reducing effective fleet capacity. Yang Ming strengthens Singapore operations Alongside its financial results, Yang Ming’s board authorised its wholly owned subsidiary, Yang Ming (Singapore) Pte. Ltd., to acquire office property in Singapore. The investment is intended to support the carrier’s long-term regional operations and strengthen its presence in one of Asia’s principal transshipment hubs. Yang Ming said it would continue monitoring cargo demand and trade flows while pursuing fleet and container renewal initiatives to improve operational efficiency and maintain its service network amid changing market conditions.

REUTERS/Hannibal Hanschke//File Photo By Holger Hansen BERLIN, Nov 11 (Reuters) – The German government will go ahead with a planned 24-terawatt-hour crisis gas reserve to be funded by user surcharges, the economy ministry said, following criticism over missed storage targets for the winter heating season this year. The state buffer, which amounts to about 10% of the nation’s gas storage capacity, will be accumulated over up to three years, the ministry said in a statement on Wednesday. It said the move would address severe disruptions, for example from acts of sabotage, and does not replace the private sector’s seasonal stock-keeping duties. “The gas reserve does not relieve market participants of their responsibilities, which include winter preparedness as well as meeting supply obligations,” it said. To fund the reserve, households would likely face 0.3% to 0.5% higher gas prices, the ministry said. Opposition parties and Italy have criticized Germany’s low gas storage levels , which stood at 62% at end-October, below a target of 70%. Berlin has said its supplies are still secure as it now has more purchasing options via liquefied natural gas terminals and through pipelines from Norway than it had in 2022 when Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine triggered an energy crisis. The government also plans a range of measures to tighten gas market regulation, including mandatory seasonal stock keeping for gas utilities, a ministry spokesperson told Reuters on Wednesday. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo By Ruth Liao and Stephen Stapczynski Nov 11, 2026 (Bloomberg) –Polish energy company Orlen SA terminated one of its long-term liquefied natural gas contracts with QatarEnergy, citing the export giant’s inability to deliver as the conflict in the Middle East disrupts shipments. The annulment is the first by a customer of QatarEnergy, which supplied about a fifth of the world’s LNG until the war between the US and Iran throttled its shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and damaged its export infrastructure. It is another blow for the emirate, as the nation’s budget deficit increases because of the lost revenue. Missile strikes in March damaged the world’s largest LNG export plant in Qatar — badly damaging two of its 14 production units and forcing the supplier to declare force majeure, a legal clause allowing producers to miss deliveries due to factors beyond their control, on shipments for the first time. Iranian attacks on vessels continue to slow shipping through Hormuz, cutting gas flows to a third of pre-war levels last month. The inability to meet contractual obligations led to the dissolving of the contract that was meant to run until 2034 and had an estimated value of €570 million ($637 million) this year, Orlen said in a statement on Tuesday. The agreement remains in force for a further 60 days. Orlen will retain a second supply contract with Qatar. Qatar sells most of its fuel under long-term contracts and has put its customers in Europe and Asia on force majeure notice for months. That’s forced buyers to replace the supply with spot cargoes, prices for which are at the highest level in years. Extended use of the clause eventually gives buyers the right to walk away, typically after a prolonged period of canceled deliveries. Qatar has been extending the measure every month, with its latest notice affecting shipments through the end of the year. Buyers are “unable to make longer term arrangements for alternative supply if their Qatari contract remains on foot, because if the volumes return at some point, it would leave the customer with an overly contracted position,” said Saul Kavonic, senior energy analyst at MST Marquee. “The longer the disruption lasts, the more customers will come under pressure to pursue this alternative.” Read More: Qatar Rewrites Its Gas Playbook With Old Tankers and New Tactics The canceled Qatari contract was Poland’s first LNG purchase agreement, paving the way for the European country to begin importing the super-chilled fuel in 2015. The contract was priced at 16% of Brent oil, according to a BloombergNEF database of LNG contracts, making it among the most expensive term deals in effect. Orlen’s second deal with Qatar is linked to natural gas benchmarks. Meanwhile, the Polish company has signed deals to procure LNG from projects in Texas and Louisiana including Port Arthur and Plaquemines — more affordable and flexible options that allows its trading desk to resell shipments. © 2026 Bloomberg L.P. articles.title: Panama Canal increases daily transit capacity to 34 slots
articles.summary: The Panama Canal has increased its daily transit capacity to 34 booking slots and raised the maximum allowable draft for vessels using the Neopanamax locks. The changes, announced on 9 November 2026, follow improvements in lake levels and more favourable hydrological forecasts. According to the Panama Canal...
articles.body: The Panama Canal has increased its daily transit capacity to 34 booking slots and raised the maximum allowable draft for vessels using the Neopanamax locks. The changes, announced on 9 November 2026, follow improvements in lake levels and more favourable hydrological forecasts. According to the Panama Canal Authority, the additional daily slot is available for Super vessels using the Panamax locks. This increases the number of slots in that category from 18 to 19. The Canal now offers 24 daily slots at the Panamax locks and 10 at the Neopanamax locks, bringing the combined total to 34. Neopanamax draft limit rises to 50 feet The Canal has also increased the maximum authorised draft for Neopanamax vessels to 15.24 metres, or 50 feet. The new limit took effect on 9 November and will remain in place until further notice. The change follows the previous increase in transit capacity and vessel draft announced in September. Under that adjustment, the Canal increased the Neopanamax draft limit to 14.94 metres and introduced a tenth daily Neopanamax transit slot from 15 October, bringing the total to 33. The latest changes provide shipping lines with greater flexibility when planning vessel deployments and cargo loading. The higher draft limit may also allow eligible containerships to carry more cargo through the waterway, depending on their operating requirements. The Panama Canal Authority said improved water conditions have made the adjustments possible. However, it will continue monitoring lake levels and hydrological forecasts before making further changes. Additional booking slot follows phased allocation schedule The new Panamax booking slot will be offered through the Canal’s Transit Reservation System. For transit dates between 12 and 17 November, the additional slot will be available during Booking Period 3 through the auction process. For transits scheduled between 18 and 23 November, the slot will be offered during Booking Period 2 under the Special Competition procedure. From 24 November onwards, the additional slot will become available through the regular opening of the Second Competition Period. The Canal Authority also reminded customers that a confirmed reservation remains the only way to guarantee a transit date. Vessels arriving without a booking may face longer waiting times, depending on traffic and available capacity. The latest adjustment provides additional transit options for container carriers and other shipping operators using the Panama Canal. However, future capacity and draft changes will continue to depend on water availability across the Canal watershed.

articles.body: Tanker Operator Furetank Nabs International Award Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 11, 2026 Image courtesy Furetank Swedish tanker operator Furetank has been named a regional winner of the EY Entrepreneur Of The Year 2026 awards, receiving the Best International Growth distinction for combining fleet expansion, technological innovation and environmental performance. The award recognizes Furetank's long-term investment strategy, which has helped position the company as a leader in developing more environmentally efficient product tankers while maintaining profitable growth. Lars Höglund, who has led the company's development for nearly four decades, accepted the award during a ceremony at Hotel Elite Park Avenue in Gothenburg. The jury highlighted Höglund's commitment to technological innovation, employee involvement and sustainable development in one of the world's most capital-intensive industries. "For almost four decades, this entrepreneur has made bold, long-term investments in one of the world's riskiest and most capital-intensive industries," the jury stated, recognizing Furetank's emphasis on safety, workplace culture and continuous improvement. Furetank's growth has been closely tied to its VINGA vessel series, developed in cooperation with FKAB Marine Design. The company and its partners have ordered 26 tankers in the series, designed to reduce the environmental footprint of petroleum product transportation. The business has grown from a family operation with a single tanker in the 1950s to a shipping company employing approximately 300 people and generating annual revenue of SEK 1.5 billion. "It all goes back to a point ten years ago when we had to renew our fleet, just as society was turning its attention to the environment," Höglund said. "Together with FKAB Marine Design, we developed a vessel design that today gives us the ships with the smallest environmental footprint in their class globally." Höglund said the fleet investment demonstrated that improved environmental performance and commercial profitability can go hand in hand. Furetank will advance to the Swedish national EY Entrepreneur Of The Year final, scheduled for January 27, 2027, at Stockholm City Hall. Image courtesy Furetank

November 11, 2026 (Credit: Baleana) British shipbuilding group Balaena and Norway's Kongsberg Maritime have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to advance the Arctic Hunter uncrewed surface vessel (USV), a proposed solution for the Royal Navy's emerging Type 92 anti-submarine warfare requirement. The agreement, signed at Kongsberg Maritime's offices in Norway on November 11, builds on an existing relationship between the companies and aims to combine British shipbuilding capabilities with Norwegian vessel design and autonomous technologies. Arctic Hunter is designed for uncrewed naval operations in extreme Arctic conditions, combining Kongsberg Maritime's commercial vessel designs and remote and autonomous technologies with sonar and military communications capabilities from UK defence technology company Thales. The proposed vessel is intended to provide persistent submarine detection capabilities in the High North, using a commercial shipbuilding approach designed to accelerate construction and delivery. Under the proposed program, the vessels would be built at Balaena's Birkenhead shipyard in the UK, with the ambition of delivering units ready for military integration before the end of the decade. The Birkenhead facility has four large dry docks, a non-tidal wet basin, fabrication facilities and a dedicated modular construction hall. Headquartered in Cornwall, Balaena employs more than 2,000 people and operates shipbuilding, repair and engineering facilities across the UK and Gibraltar, including 12 dry docks. The companies intend to use their collaboration to support the development of future naval capabilities and strengthen maritime security across the North Atlantic and High North.

November 11, 2026 Copyright Casimiro/AdobeStock New industrial AI initiative targets shipyard automation, robotics and preservation of technical expertise across Fincantieri's global shipbuilding operations. Italian shipbuilding group Fincantieri has announced a strategic partnership with Poste Italiane and telecommunications company TIM to establish Italy's first integrated national Physical AI ecosystem, designed to accelerate the application of artificial intelligence, robotics and automation in shipbuilding. The initiative, called "Fincantieri Ontology," is a central component of the company's 2026–2030 industrial plan, F4 (Fast Forward Further Future), which prioritizes digitalization, automation and the protection of industrial knowledge. The partnership combines the three companies' technological capabilities to develop a secure digital infrastructure that integrates AI directly into ship design, construction and vessel management. Fincantieri Ontology will focus on automating shipyard design and production processes, while the parallel "Navis Sapiens" initiative targets the digitalization of ships themselves, ultimately supporting increasingly autonomous vessel operations. A key element involves creating digital representations of industrial processes, capturing technical expertise and using AI models to optimize manufacturing operations. The companies plan to develop four-dimensional design and construction models, enabling shipyard workers and robotic systems to receive AI-optimized work packages and daily production instructions. The initiative supports Fincantieri's industrial workload valued at approximately $81 billion (€70 billion), extending through 2036. Its supply chain includes 7,000 small and medium-sized enterprises, 18 shipyards worldwide and approximately 100,000 people accessing its facilities daily. Another objective is preserving accumulated shipbuilding knowledge while transitioning traditional manufacturing roles toward digitally enabled production. "Data and Artificial Intelligence are the driving forces behind our 2026–2030 Industrial Plan," said Pierroberto Folgiero, CEO and General Manager of Fincantieri. "With the launch of this strategic partnership, we are not simply digitalizing an industrial process; we are documenting and protecting the ontology of our technical culture." Fincantieri said the partnership will establish a protected computing environment combining local AI processing and secure cloud infrastructure, supporting cybersecurity and safeguarding sensitive industrial data while accelerating robotics adoption across its shipbuilding operations.

November 11, 2026 Copyright metamoworks/AdobeStock AI-powered voyage optimization, autonomous port operations and maritime safety technologies headline the competition's 10th anniversary. Singapore's Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) and the National University of Singapore's NUSX announced the winners of the 2026 PIER71 Smart Port Challenge (SPC), marking the competition's 10th anniversary with a record 586 proposals from 281 startups across 39 countries. The competition, designed to accelerate maritime innovation and commercialization, attracted technologies spanning artificial intelligence, robotics, autonomous operations, cybersecurity and decarbonization. Australia's Ocean Intelligence won the Top Start-up Prize for its AI-powered voyage optimization platform, which combines ocean currents, weather conditions and vessel characteristics to identify fuel-efficient routes, reducing operating costs and emissions. South Korea's Vueron Technology received the Top Scale-up Prize for its AI-powered LiDAR perception technology supporting autonomous mobility and industrial safety. China's Trunk Technology (Beijing), which develops autonomous driving and intelligent fleet management solutions for ports, received a Special Mention. Four additional thematic awards recognized innovations in digitalization, maritime green technologies, smart ports and smart shipping. Beyond the winners, competing technologies included robotic cargo hold cleaning systems, automated confined-space inspections, AI-based maritime cybersecurity platforms and biological sensors capable of detecting water pollution. Of the submissions, 21 startups from 11 countries entered the 10-week SPC Accelerate program, with eight advancing to the Grand Finale. Letters of Intent were signed with 28 maritime companies to explore pilot projects and proof-of-concept deployments. Since launching in 2017, the Smart Port Challenge has attracted more than 2,100 proposals and supported over 200 startups through its accelerator. PIER71-supported startups have collectively raised more than S$180 million in capital since 2018. "Over the past decade, the Smart Port Challenge has brought technology start-ups and maritime companies together to develop solutions for industry needs," said Ang Wee Keong, Chief Executive of MPA. PIER71 is also expanding international commercialization support through partnerships in Hamburg, Rotterdam and Los Angeles, connecting emerging maritime technology companies with overseas markets, investors and industry partners.

articles.body: AD Ports Group reported record quarterly earnings for the third quarter of 2026, despite a sharp decline in container throughput at its UAE ports amid continued disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz. The Abu Dhabi-based group recorded revenue of AED 7.99 billion, up 48% compared with the same period last year. EBITDA increased 63% to AED 1.97 billion, while net profit rose 64% to AED 975 million. The stronger results were supported by growth across the group’s four main business clusters. Maritime & Shipping and Logistics delivered particularly strong revenue increases, while port operations recovered from the previous quarter. However, the operating environment remained challenging for terminals in the UAE, where geopolitical disruptions continued to affect cargo flows. UAE container volumes remain under pressure Container throughput at AD Ports Group’s UAE terminals fell 57% year on year to 751,000 TEU during the third quarter. Nevertheless, volumes increased by more than 30% compared with the second quarter, indicating a partial recovery from the earlier decline. Capacity utilisation at UAE container terminals improved from 22% in the second quarter to 29% in the third quarter. Meanwhile, utilisation across the group’s international terminals increased from 61% to 73%. The Ports Cluster reported revenue of AED 798 million, up 12% year on year. EBITDA rose 8% to AED 388 million. To address the disruption, AD Ports Group continued using alternative cargo routes through Fujairah Terminals and Khor Fakkan Port, located outside the Strait of Hormuz. The company also expanded land and air transport connections, alongside additional storage and warehousing facilities. These measures form part of wider efforts to maintain cargo movements between the UAE and international markets despite the regional security situation. Feeder shipping supports earnings growth AD Ports Group’s Maritime & Shipping business delivered strong results during the quarter, supported by higher freight rates and expanded capacity. Container feeder shipping volumes reached 900,000 TEU, remaining broadly unchanged from the previous year but increasing 22% compared with the second quarter. The company reported higher freight rates in its feeder operations, alongside continued growth in Ro-Ro shipping and tanker activities. Revenue in the Maritime & Shipping Cluster increased 56% year on year to AED 4.74 billion. EBITDA more than doubled to AED 1.23 billion. Meanwhile, the Logistics Cluster recorded revenue of AED 1.96 billion, representing a 76% annual increase. Its EBITDA rose 246% to AED 116 million. The group attributed the improvement partly to measures introduced to maintain supply chain connectivity across the UAE and wider Gulf region. Dr. Afif Saif Al Yafei, Group CEO of AD Ports Group, said the company had maintained its operations through one of the most challenging periods in its history. He highlighted the contribution of alternative multimodal routes and the expansion of the group’s shipping and logistics activities. The company also continued its international expansion during the quarter. It funded the acquisition of Brazilian port terminal operator Corredor Logística e Infraestrutura (CLI), which was completed on 1 October 2026. For the first nine months of 2026, AD Ports Group reported revenue of AED 20.83 billion, an increase of 41% year on year. Nine-month net profit reached AED 2.46 billion, up 64% compared with the same period in 2025. articles.summary: FEET becomes first fund to adopt updated Singapore-Asia Taxonomy, linking financing for vessel efficiency technologies to independently verified fuel and emissions savings.Singapore has taken another step toward accelerating maritime decarbonization…
articles.body: Finance Framework Opens Door to Ship Retrofit Investment Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 11, 2026 Image courtesy Singapore Sustainable Finance Association (SSFA) FEET becomes first fund to adopt updated Singapore-Asia Taxonomy, linking financing for vessel efficiency technologies to independently verified fuel and emissions savings. Singapore has taken another step toward accelerating maritime decarbonization, with the Fund for Energy Efficiency Technologies (FEET) becoming the first investment fund to adopt the revised Singapore-Asia Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (SAT), establishing a framework to direct capital toward vessel retrofits and energy efficiency technologies. The second edition of the taxonomy was announced by the Singapore Sustainable Finance Association (SSFA), supported by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), at COP31 in Türkiye on November 11, 2026 . Significantly for shipping, the revised taxonomy recognizes qualifying vessel retrofits and energy efficiency technology (EET) installations that deliver measurable greenhouse gas emissions reductions. The development expands the framework for sustainable maritime investment beyond new low-emission vessels to include technologies capable of improving the environmental performance of ships already operating. FEET, managed by AIM Horizon Investments with the Global Centre for Maritime Decarbonisation (GCMD) serving as decarbonization advisor, provides up to 100% upfront financing for qualifying efficiency technologies through a blended finance structure. The fund uses a "pay-as-you-save" model, linking shipowners' payments to independently verified fuel and regulatory savings generated by installed equipment. The initiative is supported by the Development Bank of Japan, DBS Bank and ING. A key development accompanying the taxonomy's adoption is the independent review by Lloyd's Register of GCMD's methodology for measuring fuel savings from wind-assisted propulsion systems (WAPS). The methodology builds on GCMD's pilot with Eastern Pacific Shipping aboard MV Pacific Sentinel , during which researchers collected 276 million data points over four months of commercial operations. Researchers analyzed more than 3,000 transitions between operating states, identifying 203 instances with sufficiently consistent conditions to isolate fuel savings attributable specifically to the wind sails. Lloyd's Register concluded that the methodology aligns with relevant industry standards and current best practices. For future FEET-financed installations, fuel savings will be independently verified, providing the basis for calculating shipowners' payments. "Even small gains in fuel efficiency can deliver meaningful fuel cost savings over a vessel's operating life, but financing them depends on confidence in the numbers," said Professor Lynn Loo, CEO of GCMD. "Trust in data is what accelerates adoption." Ang Wee Keong, Chief Executive of the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore, described the adoption as an important step in advancing sustainable maritime finance. For shipowners, the significance is practical: a financing structure that reduces upfront investment requirements while tying repayment to demonstrated operational savings could help accelerate adoption of proven efficiency technologies across the existing global fleet.

articles.body: A.P. Moller–Maersk has confirmed an IT security incident involving unauthorised access and data extraction from a legacy system, following claims by a hacker group that it obtained approximately 100 gigabytes of information linked to the shipping company’s logistics operations. In a statement issued on 11 November, Maersk acknowledged that an unauthorised party had accessed a local system inherited through a previous acquisition. The Danish shipping group said its cybersecurity team immediately launched an investigation and took measures to secure the affected system. The confirmation comes after a relatively unknown hacker group, WhiteArmor, claimed to have stolen extensive operational and personal information from a logistics platform associated with LF Logistics, the business acquired by Maersk in 2022. Hackers claim access to extensive logistics data According to Danish technology publication Ingeniøren, WhiteArmor claims to possess approximately 100 GB of data from a platform previously operated by LF Logistics, which is now integrated into Maersk’s warehousing and distribution operations. The group alleges that the stolen information includes 29,297 driver profiles, of which 16,093 reportedly contain plaintext passwords, alongside 16,123 employee accounts, including 33 with elevated administrative privileges. The alleged dataset also includes information relating to nearly 19,000 delivery recipients, more than 64,000 signed delivery receipts, approximately 14.44 million warehouse inventory records and hundreds of thousands of purchase orders and shipment notifications. WhiteArmor has reportedly demanded approximately US$5 million in bitcoin, threatening to disclose the information unless payment is received by 7 December. However, the authenticity and extent of the alleged data theft have not been independently verified, and Maersk has not publicly confirmed that WhiteArmor was responsible for the security incident. Maersk reports no disruption to customer operations In its official statement, Maersk said its preliminary investigation suggests that no sensitive data has been disclosed, despite confirming that data was extracted from the affected system. “Our findings so far strongly suggest no sensitive data has been disclosed,” the company stated. Maersk added that the incident appears to be isolated to the local legacy system, with no indication that other company systems or customer and partner platforms connected through APIs and electronic data interchange (EDI) have been affected. The shipping group also indicated that it does not anticipate any disruption to customer operations, with its digital platforms remaining available for booking and managing shipments. The company said it would continue investigating the incident and inform potentially affected parties if further findings make additional notifications necessary. Investigation continues as questions remain over stolen data The incident has drawn attention to potential cybersecurity vulnerabilities associated with legacy logistics platforms, particularly those incorporated into larger organisations following acquisitions. According to cybersecurity specialists cited by Ingeniøren, WhiteArmor’s allegations appear credible, although the available information suggests a possible data theft and extortion incident rather than a conventional ransomware attack involving the encryption of systems. Nevertheless, no independent confirmation has established a connection between the specific data allegedly held by WhiteArmor and the information Maersk has acknowledged was extracted. Maersk has advised customers to remain cautious about unexpected communications referencing the incident and to verify suspicious messages through their established company contacts. The investigation remains ongoing, with the full extent of the incident and any potential exposure of customer or operational information yet to be established.

articles.title: U.S. Container Imports Hit Record High as China Trade Surges, Port Delays Mount
articles.summary: October 2026 container imports reached an all-time high of 2.67 million TEUs, according to Descartes, as China-origin cargo rebounded, East and Gulf Coast ports gained ground, and global shipping faced continued uncertainty over trade policy, maritime security and critical shipping routes.U.S.
articles.body: U.S. Container Imports Hit Record High as China Trade Surges, Port Delays Mount Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 11, 2026 Source: Descartes Datamyne™ October 2026 container imports reached an all-time high of 2.67 million TEUs, according to Descartes, as China-origin cargo rebounded, East and Gulf Coast ports gained ground, and global shipping faced continued uncertainty over trade policy, maritime security and critical shipping routes. U.S. container imports surged to an all-time monthly record in October 2026, reaching 2,674,808 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs), an increase of 5% from September and 16% compared with October 2025, according to the November Global Shipping Report from Descartes Systems Group. The October total surpassed the previous record of 2,622,465 TEUs, established in May 2022, by more than 52,000 TEUs. Through the first 10 months of 2026, U.S. container imports were 2.3% ahead of the corresponding period in 2025, marking a significant turnaround after volumes trailed last year's pace through much of 2026. The results reflect sustained cargo demand, a substantial recovery in imports from China and changing cargo flows through major U.S. gateways. However, the record volumes also coincide with growing port delays, evolving trade policies and persistent geopolitical risks affecting international shipping. China Drives Import Growth China was a major contributor to October's record performance, with imports reaching 987,805 TEUs, up 6.9% from September and 22.9% year-over-year. It was the fourth consecutive monthly increase in China-origin cargo and the highest monthly volume since January 2025. China accounted for 36.9% of all U.S. container imports during October, up from 36.3% in September. Its 63,351-TEU monthly increase represented approximately half of the overall growth in U.S. imports. The largest commodity categories included plastics, at 144,530 TEUs; furniture and bedding, at 137,551 TEUs; and toys, games and sporting goods, at 102,672 TEUs. The recovery extended beyond China. Imports from the 10 largest countries of origin increased 5.8% month-over-month and 18.5% year-over-year. South Korea and Germany each recorded monthly growth of 22.8%, while all 10 leading countries posted year-over-year gains. These figures suggest that October's strength was broadly distributed across major U.S. trading partners, even as China remained the dominant source of incremental cargo growth. Source: Descartes Datamyne™ East and Gulf Coast Ports Gain Ground Cargo growth was uneven across U.S. ports, with East and Gulf Coast gateways outperforming their West Coast counterparts. Houston recorded the largest monthly increase among the 10 leading ports, gaining 42,665 TEUs, or 26.7%. Savannah followed with a 12.6% increase, while Norfolk rose 17.7% and Charleston climbed 18.6%. Combined Gulf Coast imports reached 266,905 TEUs, a 24% monthly increase and the highest level since Descartes began tracking the regional statistic in August 2023. Houston accounted for approximately 83% of the Gulf Coast's monthly increase, although Descartes cautioned that part of the rebound reflected recovery from September's weaker volumes. Meanwhile, Los Angeles imports declined 1.4%, Long Beach fell 2% and Oakland dropped 10.9%. The five leading East and Gulf Coast gateways increased their combined market share to 39.9%, compared with 36.7% in September. The five leading West Coast gateways saw their share decline from 47% to 44.9%. Port Delays Continue Climbing Despite strong throughput, port performance indicators suggest mounting pressure on cargo movements. Average transit delays across the 10 tracked gateways increased to 6.3 days in October, compared with 6.0 days in September and 4.2 days in June. That represents an approximately 50% increase over four months. Seven of the 10 ports experienced increased delays during October, with New York/New Jersey recording 8.1 days, Seattle 7.6 days and Savannah 6.9 days. Descartes warned that sustained import volumes exceeding 2.5 million TEUs monthly since July may be contributing to pressure on inland logistics networks. Source: Descartes Datamyne™ Trade Policy and Maritime Security Complicate Outlook Beyond port operations, shipping companies face several significant regulatory and geopolitical developments. The U.S. Trade Representative extended the suspension of specified Section 301 maritime fees and related duties targeting China's maritime, logistics and shipbuilding sectors through January 9, 2027, providing temporary relief while leaving longer-term cost exposure unresolved. The Panama Canal Authority increased daily Neopanamax transit slots from nine to 10 beginning October 15, bringing total daily availability across both lock systems to 33. Meanwhile, Maersk announced plans to return its India–Europe ME1 Gemini service to the Suez Canal route, although security conditions remain a determining factor. Middle East maritime security continues to present serious concerns. According to the report, the International Maritime Organization recorded 129 confirmed shipping incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and wider Middle East through November 5. Labor uncertainty also persists at Los Angeles and Long Beach, where negotiations involving port watchmen continue under a contract extension through November 20. For shipowners, carriers and cargo interests, October's record imports demonstrate the strength of U.S. container demand, but also underscore an increasingly complicated operating environment. Descartes recommends that importers closely monitor port performance, trade-policy developments, canal capacity and maritime security while maintaining flexibility in sourcing, vessel routing and inventory planning. With cargo volumes at historic highs and operational risks accumulating, the industry's challenge is not simply moving more containers, but maintaining reliable and predictable supply chains amid shifting global conditions.
